title: Ingest rate-fence and typed enrichment for usage events
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Goal: Add a lightweight, low-latency rate-fencing layer at the usage-event ingestion gateway and a typed-enrichment step prior to schema validation to reduce false rejects and protect downstream streaming pipelines.

Context: We have sporadic bursts from internal integration tests and a handful of customers that generate high fan-out telemetry. Prior incidents showed the schema-validation workers queue up and cause elevated latency and some tokenized events to be dropped. Current validators are strict and often reject events that are semantically valid but use variant typing (string vs number) for fields like 'token_count' and 'duration_ms'.

Scope:
- Implement a rate-fence per-tenant + per-route with configurable burst windows and backpressure signals to clients (HTTP 429 + Retry-After or streaming throttling hooks).
- Add a typed-enrichment pass that coerces common variant types into a canonical format, adds derived fields (billing_token_group, estimate_cost_usd) and tags (ingest_source, sdk_version) used by downstream analytics.
- Emit enriched-event + pre-validation snapshot to a short-lived buffer topic for debugging and controlled replays.
- Keep schema-validator strict mode for production; add a permissive fallback that logs anomalies and forwards to a quarantine stream for manual review.

Non-goals: Full schema evolution engine, long-term data reprocessing, or changing billing logic in this ticket.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- We favour deterministic enrichment (explicit coercions with safe defaults) over heuristic guesses to avoid semantic drift.
- Rate-fencing is implemented at the gateway (edge) to prevent wasted compute in downstream services. This increases gateway complexity but reduces overall cost during bursts.
- To avoid increased P99 latency we only perform enrichment for fields flagged in a short allowlist (token_count, duration_ms, embeddings_enabled, request_type). Additional enrichment will be gated behind feature flags.

Performance targets:
- Additional median latency at gateway: +<= 6 ms.
- Gateway must handle 50k RPS steady and 150k RPS 30s burst without dropping below SLOs for top-tier customers.
- Quarantine topic should sustain 5k RPS for anomaly inspection.

Observability & runbooks:
- Dashboards: ingest-gateway/rate-fence (latency, 429 rate by tenant), enrichment/errors, quarantine/throughput.
- Alerts: 429 rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 min, enrichment error rate > 0.1%, schema-validator backlog > 2 minutes.
- Runbook: rollback feature-flag on gateway if 429s spike across all tenants; fallback plan routes to permissive-validation path and opens an incident channel.

Acceptance criteria:
- Gateway exposes config for per-tenant burst and sustained windows; tests cover policy enforcement.
- Enrichment step converts common type variants and produces consistent enriched payloads; unit tests for coercions and derived fields.
- Integration test that simulates a 30s burst and validates downstream validators remain within SLOs.
- Documentation: Confluence design doc + developer guide for adding new enrichment rules.

Links to artifacts are in attachments.
